## Summary

Declare CFEL operator alias

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Operator//Alias == "alias(Relation//RELATION_NAME) == \"notation token\""
```

### Prose Claim

`alias(Relation//RELATION_NAME) == "notation token"` takes a qualified Relation-object address and binds that declared graph Relation's exact name to one nonempty lexical notation token in the selected effective MODEL. Resolve the name exactly; do not infer case folding or undeclared synonyms. A Relation has at most one authored alias. Reject undeclared Relation names, conflicting alias values and ambiguous token bindings. Without an alias, use the full named Relation notation.

This CFEL operator binds notation metadata; it does not construct a literal-to-Node graph Relation or equate different Relation identities. The token follows the owning Relation Declaration's directional reading and grants no endpoint permission, cardinality or second authored fact. In a graph expression, `Relation//NAME` references a Relation object as an endpoint, whereas `((NAME))` invokes that Relation between endpoints.

## Summary

Require Exactly One Defining Requirement per Model Entity

## Claim

### Prose Claim

Each logical model Entity has exactly one canonical declaring Requirement with Form Declaration in the selected effective MODEL. Its governed Subject identifies the declared entity. This applies to Objects, Aspects, graph Relation types, CFEL descriptors, Carriers and their dependent Properties; a Scope Unit does not change an Entity's identity or declaring meaning. Additional scoped Requirements may constrain an Entity without becoming additional declaring owners.

A missing declaring Requirement or multiple effective declaring Requirements fails this rule. IS_DECLARED_BY identifies the qualified declaring Atom through its GOVERNS link. Qualification requires Requirement role and Declaration form; it is not based on the retired Entity Definition or Relation Definition forms. Count inherited Current Declarations and explicit local replacements after MODEL override resolution. A replaced Declaration remains available in its base MODEL and is not a second effective owner locally. Drafts and archives are not Current owners.

For / specialization, the narrower Declaration inherits applicable broader constraints and states its differences. For // instantiation, the instance follows its kind Declaration and states instance-specific facts. Reuse applicable base structure, Properties and constraints instead of copying them. Containment adds no inheritance. A Method Atom remains an Atom with Header.Role Method. Do not create new entities for every characteristic merely to multiply Atoms; equivalent Property headings denote one logical Entity.

This exact-one invariant concerns declaring owners of model entities, not a new Requirement for every runtime instance. A minimal inverse Declaration references its canonical counterpart instead of duplicating shared meaning; a qualified non-inverse derived view retains its qualification.

## Summary

Declare IS_DECLARED_BY

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation//IS_DECLARED_BY ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Derived;

Relation//IS_DECLARED_BY ((IS_DERIVED_RELATION_OF)) Relation//GOVERNS;

# instances
$declared_subject ((IS_DECLARED_BY)) Atom/(.Header.Role: Requirement)/(.Header.Form: Declaration)//$atom
```

### Prose Claim

IS_DECLARED_BY relates a declared model entity or instance to its canonical declaring Atom, qualified by CA-R-2278. The Target has Header.Role Requirement and Header.Form Declaration. Derive this view only when that Atom's GOVERNS link identifies the declared Subject and the declaring ownership qualification is satisfied in the selected effective MODEL. An arbitrary GOVERNS link from another role or form does not produce IS_DECLARED_BY.

The Host is the qualified Declaration's governed Subject; it may be outside the Node branch. The Target is the qualified declaring Atom. This view reuses the existing direct GOVERNS fact and adds no independently stored reverse fact. Its direction reverses the selected, qualified GOVERNS fact; it is not an unconditional HAS_INVERSE binding for GOVERNS.

Forward `Host ((IS_DECLARED_BY)) Target` and reverse `Target <((IS_DECLARED_BY)) Host` are written views of that same derived fact. CA-R-1199 retains the general GOVERNS meaning. CA-R-2278 supplies the declaring ownership qualification; this Declaration retains the qualified endpoint transformation. Neither a derivation reference nor a displayed view grants permission or cardinality.

## Summary

Define Relation

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation;

Relation.** {::1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) (Relation, Relation.**);
(Relation, Relation.**) {::0+}((HAS_PROPERTY)) Relation.**;

# instances
Relation//$relation;
$relation.** {::1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) ($relation, $relation.**);
($relation, $relation.**) {::0+}((HAS_PROPERTY)) $relation.**;
```

### Prose Claim

Relation defines a reusable directed graph Relation Type with a Name and Meaning. Each actual link is a tuple (Host, Relation Type, Target); persist each direct fact once. An actual edge does not create a separate Relation ID. Endpoints are declared model Entities or instances, including Carrier and CFEL descriptors, and exclude literal values and glyphs. An operator is distinct from a graph Relation even when its notation spells a Relation traversal. Its declared descriptor may be an endpoint.

A direct Relation Declaration owns shared meaning, endpoint signature and any counterpart binding. A derived counterpart remains a distinct Relation with its own Declaration; its meaning and endpoints are inferred through that binding. An alias supplies lexical notation for one Relation; it does not create a new Relation, a Node or a separate Relation ID.

condition/test, `{>n}` is a count condition/test that compares the actual count

nested children.

name count aggregates selected distinct descendant Property identities under p
within each selected bearer; it does not count direct values or another
bearer's descendants.

counts. The first constrains outgoing Relation instances per selected Source;
the second constrains reverse links per selected Target. Reversing the written

IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR binds an inverse alias model address to its canonical Relation model address. This binding infers no bounds, grants no endpoint permission and creates no second authored Relation fact.

## Summary

Declare Atom.Header.Container

## Claim

### Prose Claim

Header.Container identifies the Atom's immediate Container.

Header.Container contains exactly one key: `atom` names the containing Atom by its base Atom ID, or `scope_unit` names the containing Scope Unit by its stable ID. A base Atom ID selects Current by default.

For a root Project Declaration Atom, an omitted Header.Container has the effective default mapping with `scope_unit` equal to `CA-SU--1`, identifying the predefined Scope Unit `world`. An explicit valid value overrides that default.
Header.Container is the sole stored Atom-containment value.
### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Atom.Header.Container{::1} :: []{::0};

Atom.Header.Container.*[in(atom,scope_unit)]{::1};

# instances
Atom//$atom;
$atom.Header.Container{::1}
```

## Summary

Declare IS_ORDERED_RIGHT_AFTER

## Claim

### Prose Claim

The Host and Target are declared model Properties of the same immediate bearer, selected from the applicable Atom.Header or Atom.Content Property structure. The Host follows the Target immediately in the declared sibling order. Ordering is acyclic; each Property has at most one immediate predecessor and at most one immediate successor. The inverse alias IS_ORDERED_RIGHT_BEFORE reverses that reading; it denotes the same ordering fact.

`x ;> y` means x is immediately before y, in the order x; y. `x <; y` means x is immediately after y, in the order y; x. These Relations specify model Property order; they do not create runtime Property instances or copy facts.

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
$host ((IS_ORDERED_RIGHT_AFTER)) $target;

Relation//IS_ORDERED_RIGHT_BEFORE ((IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR)) Relation//IS_ORDERED_RIGHT_AFTER;

alias(Relation//IS_ORDERED_RIGHT_AFTER) == "<;";

alias(Relation//IS_ORDERED_RIGHT_BEFORE) == ";>"
```

## Semantics

IS_ORDERED_RIGHT_AFTER relates a model Property to its immediately preceding sibling Property.
